strengths: Clear and well-motivated problem formulation distinguishing query circuits from capability circuits, addressing a genuine gap in input-level LLM explanations
Robust NDF metric that addresses real numerical instability issues with NFS on complex datasets, with mathematical soundness and empirical validation across multiple datasets
Insightful observation that paraphrases can enable successful circuit discovery where direct queries fail, elegantly motivating the BoN sampling approach

Comprehensive experimental validation across diverse datasets (IOI, arithmetic, MMLU-9 categories, ARC) with consistent improvements and thorough ablations showing how different factors affect performance
Practical engineering contributions with iBoN and BoN-CSM variants addressing computational bottlenecks, and detailed experimental setup enabling reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty in core method: BoN is essentially trying multiple input variants and selecting the best, which is straightforward despite being effective
Fundamental limitations left unaddressed: neglect of combinatorial edge interactions and restriction to single-token outputs severely constrain applicability to real-world multi-token generation
Lacks actual interpretation of discovered circuits—while circuits are identified, their computational roles remain unexplained, undermining practical utility for understanding model decisions

Modest empirical improvement: 60% performance recovery with 1.3% edges on MMLU, and complement circuits show near-random performance (Figure A12), raising questions about whether discovered circuits capture genuine mechanisms

Paraphrase dependency and scalability concerns: requires GPT-4o for paraphrase generation reducing reproducibility, per-query cost remains substantial (132s), and limited analysis of sensitivity to paraphrase quality and diversity
Narrow experimental scope: only tested on small models (1.3B, GPT-2 Small), restricted to MCQ single-token predictions, and lacks comparison with criticized surrogate approaches (SAEs, CLTs)
Limited theoretical understanding of why BoN works: explanations rely on plausible but unproven assumptions about gradient noise and lottery tickets; no principled guidance on paraphrase selection
Statistical rigor issues: no confidence intervals or significance tests, varying query counts across categories, no variance analysis across random seeds or paraphrase selections

strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation distinguishing query circuits from capability circuits and surrogate-based approaches
NDF metric robustly addresses documented instability of NFS on general datasets with proper mathematical grounding and broad applicability
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets (IOI, arithmetic, MMLU, ARC) with scaling to larger models (GPT-2 XL, Llama-3-8B)
Thorough ablations and complementary analyses including shared sub-circuit discovery, complement circuits, and runtime comparisons
Honest discussion of limitations (combinatorial effects, single-token restriction, incomplete SAE representations) and validation of circuit actionability through bias reduction experiments
Detailed reproducibility information with extensive appendices and multiple design choice justifications
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty—core approach builds primarily on existing methods (EAP-IG, indirect effects); using paraphrases for perturbation is intuitive but lacks theoretical grounding
NDF is a straightforward mathematical transformation of NFS (clipping and reversal), derived from recently-introduced CMD metric rather than independently motivated
Insufficient theoretical understanding of why BoN succeeds—attributed to 'gradient noise and combinatorial effects' without rigorous validation or formal analysis of paraphrase-based perturbation
Severely limited practical utility—60% performance recovery on MMLU leaves 40% of behavior unexplained; circuits remain large (1.3% of edges) and opaque without manual inspection
Scope constraints: restricted to single-token predictions, evaluated only on curated tasks with simple reformulation patterns; unclear scalability to open-ended generation or longer reasoning

Missing comparisons with related work (no direct Circuit Tracing comparison, limited baseline ablations) and incomplete analysis (circuit variance across query types, cross-model generalization, per-query quality statistics)
Experimental design choices inadequately justified: paraphrase count (p=9), external dependency on GPT-4o for generation, MMLU category selection biased by Claude performance
Application beyond bias reduction not demonstrated; actionability claims rest on limited study (Section 6.5); no evidence circuits enable meaningful interventions or transfer between similar queries
